The paper proposes an automatic workflow for assessing damage on gas turbine blades using deep learning on borescope video feeds.
The workflow uses a Mask R-CNN network with a PointRend module for instance segmentation to detect and classify different types of blade damage.
The network is trained to detect five damage classes: casing, compressor-rotor, surface-damage, material-separation, and material-deformation.
Out of 4881 video frames, 104 images were manually labelled, with 89 used for training and 15 used for testing.
The network achieves better instance segmentation performance after 2000 training iterations compared to 500 iterations, as measured by mAP and mean matched IoU.
A post-processing step is introduced that applies a high-pass filter and mask erosion to highlight small-scale surface features and discontinuities missed by the network.
The algorithm tracks blades across video frames and calculates the damage area as a fraction of the projected blade area for each blade.
The blade tracking algorithm assumes blades do not move significantly across adjacent frames and travel approximately horizontally.
The PointRend module is added to the Mask R-CNN network to improve segmentation accuracy, particularly for smaller objects like surface damage marks.

The two key performance metrics used to evaluate the instance segmentation results are mean average precision (mAP) and mean matched intersection-over-union (IoU), calculated at an IoU threshold of 0.5.
The automatic workflow removes human biases, enables faster decision-making, and can quantify uncertainty via confidence scores.
The workflow extends previous work on semantic segmentation of borescope images by classifying multiple types of damage and tracking individual blades across video frames.
The authors note that the introduction of manual labelling may involve biases, but argue that the automatic framework should mitigate the impact of these biases compared to a fully manual procedure.
The authors find that the testing loss is not an adequate metric for judging the quality of the network, as it does not penalize missing detections severely enough.
The authors demonstrate the workflow on two borescope videos of high-pressure compressor blades, one with 97 blades and the other with 38 blades.
